observation_summary: The compiler failed to correctly identify module names when file paths contained backslashes (common on Windows), leading to incorrect module name generation and dependency resolution errors.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved adding a normalization step to replace backslashes with forward slashes in the filename before processing. This is a correction to the internal computational procedure used to derive module names from file paths. It is not a simple value assignment, nor a missing guard (Checking), but a refinement of the string processing algorithm to ensure consistent input for the module naming logic.
evidence_used: The fix adds 'filename = filename.replace("\\", "/");' to the 'normalizeSourceName' method.
The failing test 'testGuessModuleName' expected 'module$baz' but received 'module$foo\baz', indicating the path processing logic was failing to handle backslashes correctly.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not just assigning a value, but performing a transformation (normalization) on the input string to correct the computational logic.
There is no missing guard or conditional check; the logic itself was insufficient for the input format.
